title: carduus pycnocephalus subsp. albidus
intro: Carduus pycnocephalus subsp. albidus, commonly known as White-headed Thistle, is a subspecies of flowering plant in the sunflower family, characterized by its white or pale purple flowers and prickly leaves. The plant has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, providing various health benefits such as reducing inflammation and improving liver function. The therapeutic actions of Carduus pycnocephalus subsp. albidus include its ability to act as a hepatoprotective agent, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory, making it a potential treatment for conditions like liver diseases and arthritis. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, alkaloids, and saponins, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and contribute to its potential therapeutic applications.
